hints: To judge one node you need the heights of both its subtrees. Can you get the heights and the verdict in the same walk?
Use a post-order DFS that returns the subtree's height, or -1 as a signal that something below is already unbalanced. The -1 then passes straight up to the root.

1. check(null) returns 0.
  2. Get the left result; if it is -1, return -1.
  3. Get the right result; if it is -1, return -1.
  4. If the two heights differ by more than 1, return -1.
  5. Otherwise return 1 + max; the tree is balanced if the root's result is not -1.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: At every node, call a separate height function on both children and compare.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One bottom-up pass returns height and failure together, so every node is visited once.

explain: In [10,5,15,null,null,12,20], node 5 has height 1 and node 15 (with children 12 and 20) has height 2. They differ by 1, so the root is fine and the answer is true. In [10,5,null,3,null,1] the tree is a left chain 10-5-3-1. At node 5 the left height is 2 and the right height is 0, a gap of 2, so it returns -1 and that -1 rides up to the root: false. Remember the rule must hold at every node, not just the root.
recognize: "Heights must differ by at most 1 at every node" → one post-order DFS returning height or a failure sentinel.
